sections.title: General subject vs. specific material
sections.content: You already know the difference between indefinite ("something in general") and definite ("a specific, known thing") conjugation from Hungarian Food. tanul works the same way: tanulok történelmet ("I study history", in general) uses the indefinite; tanulom a történelmet ("I'm studying the history [material]", this particular content) uses the definite, matching the definite article a/az.

items.spanish: Ma este tanulom a történelmet a vizsgára.
items.english: Tonight I'm studying the history material for the exam.

sections.content: If the noun has a/az in front of it, or you mean a specific, already-identified chunk of material, switch to the definite form: tanulom, not tanulok.
